# Altair-Vega Python Code for Seattle Weather Dataset

Here are several examples of visualizing the Seattle weather dataset using Altair:

## Basic Setup

```python
import altair as alt
from vega_datasets import data

# Load the Seattle weather dataset
source = data.seattle_weather()
```

## 1. Simple Bar Chart (Precipitation by Month)

```python
alt.Chart(source).mark_bar().encode(
    x='month(date):T',
    y='mean(precipitation):Q'
).properties(
    title='Average Precipitation by Month'
)
```

## 2. Line Chart (Temperature Over Time)

```python
alt.Chart(source).mark_line().encode(
    x='date:T',
    y='temp_max:Q'
).properties(
    title='Maximum Temperature Over Time',
    width=600,
    height=300
)
```

## 3. Scatter Plot (Temperature vs Precipitation)

```python
alt.Chart(source).mark_circle().encode(
    x='temp_max:Q',
    y='precipitation:Q',
    color='weather:N',
    tooltip=['date', 'weather', 'temp_max', 'precipitation']
).properties(
    title='Temperature vs Precipitation by Weather Type'
)
```

## 4. Interactive Multi-View Dashboard

```python
brush = alt.selection_interval()

points = alt.Chart(source).mark_point().encode(
    x='temp_min:Q',
    y='temp_max:Q',
    color=alt.condition(brush, 'weather:N', alt.value('lightgray'))
).add_params(brush)

bars = alt.Chart(source).mark_bar().encode(
    x='count()',
    y='weather:N',
    color='weather:N'
).transform_filter(brush)

points & bars
```

## 5. Heatmap (Daily Patterns)

```python
alt.Chart(source).mark_rect().encode(
    x='date(date):O',
    y='month(date):O',
    color='temp_max:Q'
).properties(
    title='Temperature Heatmap'
)
```

---

These examples use Altair's declarative syntax with the built-in `seattle-weather.csv` from vega_datasets.
